scenes.title: Where configuration lives
scenes.narration: Deslop is configured with a committed .deslop.toml next to your code: what to skip, what to hide, and when to fail CI. It is looked up next to the scan root, or you can point at any file with dash-dash-config. A missing config is not an error; built-in rules apply.
scenes.excerpt:
Deslop looks for `.deslop.toml` **next to the scan root** — the directory you point it at. Point it elsewhere with `--config`:

```bash
deslop .                          # uses ./.deslop.toml if present
deslop ./src --config ci.toml     # explicit config, any name
```

A missing config is not an error — Deslop runs with the built-in rules below.

scenes.title: exclude versus report_hide
scenes.narration: exclude drops a file before analysis — never parsed, never fingerprinted. report_hide keeps it in analysis but marks occurrences hidden; a cluster drops from the report only when all its members are hidden. So generated code duplicating itself stays out of the headline, while hand-written code duplicating a generated file still surfaces.
scenes.excerpt:
| `exclude` | The file is **dropped before analysis** — never parsed, never fingerprinted. | Vendored code, build output, anything you never want compared. |
| `report_hide` | The file **is analysed**, but every occurrence is marked hidden. A cluster is dropped from the report **only when all of its members are hidden**. | Generated code. You still want to know when *hand-written* code duplicates a generated file. |

scenes.title: CLI precedence
scenes.narration: A flag always wins over the matching config key for that run. For the threshold: dash-dash-no-fail-over, then dash-dash-fail-over, then the max_duplication_percent key, then off. For split-by-language, the flag or the config key — either enables it. For ranking, the VS Code extension setting overrides .deslop.toml.
scenes.excerpt:
When the same setting comes from more than one place, this is who wins:

- **Threshold:** `--no-fail-over` → `--fail-over <n>` → `[threshold] max_duplication_percent` → off.
- **Split by language:** the `--split-by-language` flag **or** `[report] split_by_language` — either one enables it.
- **Ranking (`structural_only`):** the VS Code extension setting overrides `.deslop.toml`.

scenes.title: Thresholds — the CI gate
scenes.narration: max_duplication_percent is a float from zero to one hundred. When repo-wide duplication exceeds it, deslop exits three and fails CI. It is the only opt-in failure path: with no threshold block and no dash-dash-fail-over, deslop always exits zero. On exit three, the full report is still written so offenders can be surfaced.
scenes.excerpt:
| `max_duplication_percent` | float | `0.0`–`100.0` | When repo-wide `duplication_percent` exceeds this, `deslop` exits **`3`** and fails CI. |

This is the **only** opt-in failure path. With no `[threshold]` block (and no `--fail-over`), `deslop` always exits `0` no matter how much duplication it finds.
